Unlike standard 2D transfer functions that map directly to color and opacity, this method interpolates between discrete styles defined in a style function texture [S1][S2, unofficial].

The claim states that the method interpolates between discrete styles defined in a style function texture, unlike standard 2D transfer functions that map directly to color and opacity. The evidence in both S1 and S2 explicitly describes a process where a 2D transfer function texture stores indices (ix, iy) which are used to look up style indices in an index function texture. These style indices are then used to perform lookups into a 'style function texture' (sft) to retrieve color and opacity values, which are then combined via bilinear interpolation. This confirms that the method relies on interpolating between discrete styles defined in a texture, rather than a direct mapping from input attributes to final color/opacity values as in standard transfer functions.
